#seniorhealth #kidneyhealth #nocturia #bladder 
Over 60? The REAL Reason You Wake Up to Pee at Night (Most Seniors Don't Know!)

Waking up at night to pee after 60? You’re not alone. Up to six in ten older adults get up two or more times a night. 

In this video, I walks through a research-checked nighttime routine for nocturia: when to drink, how salt can affect night trips, how to make the walk to the bathroom safer, why your pill list and kidney safety matter, and why your bladder may not be the real cause. We cover sleep apnea, bladder diaries, red-flag symptoms like blood in the urine, and five questions to ask your doctor. Sources include the CDC, NIH/NLM, Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine, and published studies. Where evidence is limited, we say so.

📚 Research References:
▪Nocturia is very common (Bosch & Weiss, J Urol, 2010).
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20620...
▪The mechanism is often overnight urine production, not the bladder (Varilla, Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine, 2011; StatPearls/NCBI).
https://community.the-hospitalist.org...
▪Kidney disease is silent (CDC, updated March 2026).
https://www.cdc.gov/kidney-disease/ph...
▪NSAIDs and kidneys (NIDDK guidance as summarized by Express Scripts, March 2026; NKF).
https://www.express-scripts.com/pharm...

▪▪▪ What Is the REAL Ideal Blood Pressure After 65?
